passage:
In media class, students watched a video of a famous person saying something shocking. Then the teacher revealed that the video was fake.
Students were disturbed because the mouth and voice looked real. The teacher explained deepfake technology and why it can be dangerous.
The class learned to check sources, look for trusted reports, and avoid sharing videos only because they cause strong emotions.
One student said, "Seeing is no longer always believing."
The teacher answered, "Seeing was never enough. Now it is even less enough."
The lesson made students understand that media literacy must grow as technology grows.
